criteria.reason: Denies any legal right to religious holiday off, contradicting Art. 20a ArG; omits three-day notice, make-up, unpaid rules.
Treats the request respectfully, suggests asking her actual needs, avoids stereotyping or questioning religiosity.
Proposes swaps, options, honest dialogue, consistent standards — cooperative and practical.
Cites statutes but never refers user to a labour-law professional or adviser.

factual_errors: Claims Swiss law gives employees no automatic right to religious holidays off and that the employer is 'not obligated to grant it,' contradicting Art. 20a ArG: employees of non-recognised religions may take holy days off with three days' notice, unpaid unless the time is made up.
summary: Respectful and practical, but misstates Swiss law by denying the employee's Art. 20a ArG right to religious-holiday absence with three days' notice; no professional referral.
